### Phase 1 first-pass: static vs declarative decomposition

Before building any marketplace, we need the renderer. Reference resume: `91b07dfb-24f2-47da-ac76-326292184c66` (viewable at `/resumes/:id` full-page, and `/embedded/resumes/:identifier` as an embed inside job/people profiles).

**Static (fixed platform chrome — never templated):**

| Piece | Why it stays static |
|---|---|
| `Sidebar`, `Navigation`, `Footer` in `ResumeDetail` | Platform IA — consistent across the app |
| `AuthOverlay` blur + sign-up prompt for anonymous users | Platform paywall, not a template concern |
| Privacy badge (`public` / `recruiter_only` / `connections` / `private`) | Derived from user record, not template data |
| `ResumeActionsMenu` (edit / add media / share / download / change privacy / promote / delete) | Owner-only platform actions |
| `ResumeTimelines` cross-section tabs (Work+Education+Volunteer merged) | Platform-level analytical view, not user-authored content |
| Video carousel (merges `resume.metaData` videos + `studioVideos` from Studio API) | Logic-heavy — studio service integration, YouTube URL conversion, index state |
| `MetadataModal` + "Add Media" flow | Platform CRUD, only visible to owner |
| Toast notifications + loading/404 states | Platform UX |
| Embedded-mode removal of chrome (`EmbeddedResume` page) | Platform decision based on route, not template |

**Declarative (controlled by template descriptor — marketplace can publish these):**

| Piece | Template-controlled |
|---|---|
| Hero layout | `split` (2-col with video) / `stacked` / `compact` |
| Hero gradient colors + accent color | theme tokens |
| Whether to show avatar / contact buttons / summary / video in hero | booleans |
| Section order | explicit array in descriptor |
| Section enablement (work, education, skills, languages, projects, volunteer, awards, certificates, publications, interests, references) | booleans |
| Section title override (e.g. "Career" instead of "Work Experience") | string |
| Section icon (whitelist of lucide icons) | string key |
| Section layout variant | `timeline` / `cards` / `grid` / `list` / `compact` |
| Grid column count for grid layouts (skills, languages, interests) | 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 |
| Whether to expand highlights by default | boolean |
| Sort order for each section | `date_desc` / `date_asc` / `manual` |
| Card style | `elevated` / `flat` / `bordered` / `ghost` |
| Section title size | `sm` / `md` / `lg` / `xl` |

### Descriptor schema (v1.2)

v1.2 adds **component blocks** — any reusable React component (e.g. `ResumeTimelines`) can be dropped into the descriptor's `sections` array alongside data-backed section blocks. Adding a new component to the registry is a one-line change in `frontend/lib/resume-template-components.ts`.

```ts
type ResumeBlock = SectionBlock | ComponentBlock;

interface ComponentBlock {
  kind: "component";
  component: "career-timeline";    // whitelist key
  enabled: boolean;
  id?: string;                     // for sidebar referencing; defaults to component key
  title?: string;                  // optional heading; omit for headless widget
  icon?: TemplateIconKey;
  props?: Record<string, unknown>; // component-specific options
}
```

Sidebar referencing (`layout.sidebar`) is now `string[]` of block ids — accepts either a section key (`"skills"`) or a component id (`"career-timeline"`), so components can live in the sidebar just like sections.

Currently registered components:

| Key | Backed by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `career-timeline` | `ResumeTimelines` | Cross-section Overview / Work / Volunteer / Education / Certificates tabs with totals |



After reviewing competitor template galleries (Resume-Now, Kickresume, Canva), v1's pure layout toggles weren't enough — industry templates differ by **named style bundles**: font family, heading style, color palette, document vs. hero mode, single vs. two-column. v1.1 adds these dimensions:

```ts
type SectionKey = "work" | "education" | "volunteer" | "skills" | "languages"
  | "projects" | "awards" | "certificates" | "publications" | "interests" | "references";

type ThemeKey = "hired-purple" | "iron-gray" | "balanced-blue" | "trusted-taupe"
  | "assertive-asphalt" | "warm-amber" | "executive-navy" | "minimal-slate";

interface ResumeTemplateDescriptor {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  industry?: string;                                     // display label
  version: "1.1";
  documentMode: "hero" | "print";                        // gradient header vs. paper document
  theme: {
    themeKey: ThemeKey;                                  // named palette (pre-baked Tailwind classes)
    fontFamily: "sans" | "serif" | "mono";
    headingStyle: "underlined" | "divider" | "caps" | "plain";
    density: "compact" | "comfortable" | "spacious";
    cardStyle?: "elevated" | "flat" | "bordered" | "ghost";
    sectionTitleSize?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl";
  };
  layout: {
    columns: 1 | 2;                                      // 2 = sidebar + main
    sidebar?: SectionKey[];                              // which sections go in the sidebar
  };
  hero: {
    enabled: boolean;
    layout: "split" | "stacked" | "compact";
    showAvatar: boolean;
    showContactButtons: boolean;
    showSummary: boolean;
    showVideo: boolean;
  };
  sections: Array<{
    key: SectionKey;
    enabled: boolean;
    title?: string;
    icon?: string;                                       // whitelist key
    layout: "timeline" | "cards" | "grid" | "list" | "compact";
    columns?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4;
    showHighlights?: boolean;
    sortBy?: "date_desc" | "date_asc" | "manual";
  }>;
}
```

**Themes are pre-baked** Tailwind class bundles — not dynamic interpolation — since Tailwind JIT can't see template strings. Registry: `frontend/lib/resume-template-themes.ts`.

### Industry presets shipped

| ID | Industry | Document mode | Theme | Font | Headings | Columns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hired-default` | All | hero | hired-purple | sans | plain | 1 |
| `payroll-iron-gray` | Finance / Payroll | print | iron-gray | serif | divider | 2 (sidebar: skills/edu/certs/lang) |
| `risk-asphalt` | Risk / Consulting | print | assertive-asphalt | sans | caps | 2 (sidebar: skills/lang/certs) |
| `executive-taupe` | Executive / C-Suite | print | trusted-taupe | serif | divider | 1 |
| `intern-education-first` | Intern / New Grad | print | balanced-blue | sans | underlined | 1 (education first) |
| `hospitality-amber` | Hospitality / Retail | print | warm-amber | sans | caps | 1 |
| `creative-minimal` | Creative / Product | print | minimal-slate | mono | plain | 1 |

The `hired-default` reproduces the current `ResumeDetail` pixel-close (gradient hero, timeline sections, split video). Print-mode presets render a paper-style document (centered name + contact line, no gradient, section headings per theme style).

### Sample resume + Template Gallery

A canonical showcase resume lives at [frontend/lib/sample-resume.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/sample-resume.ts) — real content derived from a user-submitted JsonResume file, enriched across every section (Skills / Languages / Certificates / Projects / Awards / Interests) so every template block renders meaningfully regardless of which preset is applied. This file is the single source-of-truth for all template previews.

**Template Gallery** on Home ([components/resume-renderer/TemplateGallery.tsx](hired.video/frontend/components/resume-renderer/TemplateGallery.tsx)) — grid of `TemplateCard`s, each rendering a miniature live preview of the sample resume in that template (via a scaled `DeclarativeResumeRenderer`, not a static image, so previews stay in sync with descriptor changes). Mounted on both authenticated and marketing variants of Home.

Each card offers:
- **Preview** → `/resumes/VIEWER/sample?template=:id` — opens the viewer with the sample resume and pre-selected preset
- **Use Free** (when `priceCents === 0`) → unlocks immediately via `unlockTemplate()` in [lib/template-unlocks.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/template-unlocks.ts)
- **Add to Cart** (when `priceCents > 0`) → pushes a `type: "template"` item into the existing cart context; standard checkout flow applies

Unlocks are tracked client-side in `localStorage` as a first pass; server-backed ownership (`templateLicenses` table) lands with the marketplace phase.

### Preview route

- `GET /resumes/VIEWER/:id` — first-pass preview page:
  - Loads the same resume via the three fallback endpoints (`getResumeById` → `getResumeForEmbed` → `getPublicResume`)
  - Renders `<DeclarativeResumeRenderer resume descriptor />` against a default descriptor that matches `ResumeDetail`
  - "Template" dropdown lists all industry presets
  - "Export" dropdown offers PDF, Word (.doc), Plain Text, Raw JSON
  - Right-side drawer with a live descriptor JSON editor — tweak and re-render instantly
  - Retains platform chrome (Sidebar, Navigation, Footer, AuthOverlay for logged-out)
- `GET /resumes/VIEWER/:id?print=1` — bare print variant:
  - No chrome, no toolbar — just the rendered resume
  - Auto-calls `window.print()` 400ms after load
  - Reads descriptor from `sessionStorage` under `resume-descriptor:{id}` so the caller's selected template survives the new-window hop
- The same `<DeclarativeResumeRenderer>` will later back `ResumeDetail`, `EmbeddedResume` (compact variant), and marketplace previews — one renderer, three hosts.

### Export formats

| Format | Mechanism | Bundle impact |
|---|---|---|
| **PDF** | Opens `?print=1` in a new window → auto-triggers browser print-to-PDF | zero |
| **Word (.doc)** | Emits Word-compatible HTML with MS Office XML namespaces, served as `application/msword` — Word opens it as a fully-styled document. True `.docx` would need a library (docx/html-docx-js); skipping for first pass. | zero |
| **Plain Text (.txt)** | JS serializer walking `ResumeData` — bulleted sections, headings, date ranges | zero |
| **Raw JSON (.json)** | `JSON.stringify(resume.data, null, 2)` | zero |

All four are implemented in `frontend/lib/resume-exporters.ts`. PDF export stashes the current descriptor in `sessionStorage` before opening the print window so the template selection survives the new-tab hop.

### Open questions (decide before Phase 1)

1. Do user-published resume templates require review before public listing, or auto-publish with report/takedown? (Voice marketplace auto-publishes — precedent says yes.)
2. Should template price be creator-set or platform-tiered ($0 / $4.99 / $9.99 / $19.99)? Tiered is simpler for tax and reduces race-to-zero.
3. Do we gate *selling* behind Pro ($9.95/mo), or allow free users to list with higher platform fee (e.g. 30% free / 20% Pro)?
4. PDF rendering path — server-side Puppeteer on CF Workers is not viable; need a separate Node service or third-party (react-pdf, DocRaptor).

### Success metrics

- GMV from template licenses (monthly)
- Creator activation rate (users who publish ≥1 template / total Pro users)
- Template application rate (licenses acquired / marketplace views)
- Top-of-funnel: anonymous visits to `/creators/earn` → signups

## Go-Live Readiness — CxO Gap Analysis

Executive view of what blocks production launch, organized by functional owner. Each finding cross-references the detail entries in the Consolidated Gap Register below. Last updated **2026-04-25**.

**Overall verdict:** The platform is **feature-rich and architecturally sound**, but launch readiness is gated by a tight cluster of legal, payout, and observability gaps that are individually small but collectively non-negotiable. The fastest path to live is a **scoped Day-1 launch** focused on the Pro / job-seeker / employer path, deferring the creator-monetization rails (articles, courses, partner program) until the payout pipeline is real.

### CEO — Strategic Readiness

**Strong**
- Positioning is coherent post-AI-CHRO redesign (#93). One product anchor ("your AI CHRO") that the rest of the surface area hangs off.
- Pricing is decisive: Free + Pro at $9.95/mo with itemized token packs ($3.99–$199.99). No Enterprise upsell to manage at launch.
- 95/5 rev-share standardised across every monetisation surface (#156). Creators see the same number everywhere.

**Risks**
- **Surface-area sprawl.** The roadmap covers jobs, recruiter CRM, ATS, video studio, voice marketplace, creator services, courses, articles, ad campaigns, partner program, outplacement, white-label, and B2B sales persona. No public commitment yet to a Day-1 wedge — "we ship everything" creates a positioning that doesn't fit a single buyer.
- **Bus factor.** Most P0/P1 surfaces are single-author. Recommend a written ownership map per surface before launch.
- **No public roadmap or changelog** for users; everything lives in this README.

### CFO — Revenue, Billing, and Payouts

**Strong**
- Payment provider abstraction with both **Stripe and Helcim** implementations (#47). Switchable via env var.
- Annual billing with 20% discount, 14-day trial, churn/cancellation/pause flow, AI usage metering, ad revenue tracking, seat-based company billing — all wired (#21–#67).
- Token-based AI metering replaces per-request rate limiting. Itemised token pack purchases live.

**Risks (go-live blockers)**
- **Partial payout pipeline.** ⚠️ Onboarding + ledger landed 2026-05-17 (#771): creators connect via Helcim ACH (tokenised bank, we never see routing/account) or Tremendous gift cards, accruals route through `PayoutLedgerService` (append-only double-entry; balance = SUM(amount_cents)), schema-drift fix dropped duplicate payout columns from `creator_profiles`, AES-GCM tax-ID encryption (#772) replaced the plaintext placeholder. **Still blocking:** #773 release worker (cron) that turns "balance ≥ $50 threshold" into actual `provider.createPayout()` calls — without it creators onboard and accrue but no money moves. Ship #773 before opening monetisation to a wider cohort.
- **No 1099 / W-9 / VAT compliance** in scope. W-9 / W-8BEN inputs land via PATCH `/me/payout-profile` (encrypted-at-rest as of #772) but year-end PDF / IRS-filing pipeline does not exist (#777 opened). US creators with >$600 lifetime settled payouts trigger 1099-NEC; international creators trigger W-8BEN; EU buyers trigger VAT MOSS. The reporting half is still unscoped.
- **Sales tax** on token packs and subscription is not visibly computed. Stripe Tax integration not detected.
- **#96 Enrichment credits** marketed as a Pro add-on but external provider is stubbed. Either ship behind a feature flag or hide the marketing.

### CTO — Engineering & Operations

**Strong**
- Drizzle schema is event-log first, polymorphic where it matters (reviews 0032, boosts 0034, feed subjects 0033). ~230 tables, 75+ migrations.
- BillingFacade + AccessPolicy split (#150) gives clean tier vs. audience semantics.
- OpenAPI 3.1 spec at `/api/openapi.json`, structured JSON logging, KV + in-process caching with explicit invalidation.
- TS strict across `api/`, `frontend/`, and `shared/`. Clean compile at the time of writing.
- Hono on Cloudflare Workers — predictable cold-start, predictable cost.

**Risks**
- **Test coverage gap (#1, still Open).** Only the BillingFacade/AccessPolicy module and a handful of tool handlers have unit tests (~264 passing). Most route handlers have **no automated coverage at all** — TS strict + manual smoke is the only safety net. **Block:** before launch, add at least smoke-level integration tests against `createApp()` for auth, billing, resume CRUD, job CRUD, and the creator opt-in flow.
- **No real-time transport.** `#41` (WebSocket chat) still Open. Recruiter↔candidate messaging works over REST but has no presence/typing/instant delivery. Acceptable for v1 if you set the expectation.
- **No background payout / reconciliation worker.** Cron exists for follow-ups, drip emails, and job-board scraping. Nothing yet for creator payouts (see CFO).
- **No documented runbook** for DB backup/restore, incident response, or secret rotation. Repo has the code; ops procedures are tribal.
- **Single-region.** Cloudflare Workers + Hyperdrive provides edge cache, but Postgres is single-region. Latency tail for APAC users is unmeasured.

### CPO — Product Completeness

**Strong**
- **Creator Program (post-2026-04-25 refactor #190)** is now coherent: per-program enrollment for Video / Voice / Services with proper event-log lifecycle, per-program legal terms, and a single management surface at `/services`.
- **Studio** has near-complete Wistia/Riverside parity per the capability matrix earlier in this README.
- **AI CHRO copilot** is the strongest single product surface and a clear anchor for the homepage CTA.
- **Marketplace + UnifiedSearch** integration (#191–#194) consolidated three previously-separate surfaces (Sell Hub, Creators browse, Search) into one navigation node.

**Risks**
- **Voice/Resume/Video template creator opt-in flows (#158, #159)** still Open. Voice clones already have a consent flow; templates do not. Creators can't yet monetise resume or video templates.
- **Courses (#160–#168)**, **Articles + Partner Program (#170–#175)**, and **Affiliate Network (#178)** are entirely greenfield. They should not be marketed at launch.
- **Pitch-deck reviewer feedback loop (#184–#186)** is the missing half of the agency v1 product. Don't market agency-tier without it.
- **Universal content rating widget (#181)** — backend done, no React widget. Listing cards have no social proof.
- **Outplacement (#100)** and **B2B Sales Persona (#104)** are P1/P2 but irrelevant to Day 1.

### CMO — Marketing Readiness

**Strong**
- Landing pages, Pricing, and Marketplace categories are **internally consistent** and accurate to current implementation (audited 2026-04-25 — see verdict in this PR's marketing audit).
- AI CHRO branding is coherent across `Index.tsx`, the chat panel header, and the system prompt.
- Marketplace category list matches `UnifiedSearch` filter pills exactly.

**Risks**
- **SEO content engine (#81)** is technically Done but light on editorial voice. Auto-generated resume/salary guides are SEO furniture, not authoritative content. No editorial cadence is defined.
- **Affiliate program (#74)** ships with tier math but creator-facing analytics are limited.
- **`isPlatformService=true` not yet flipped** on any seeded service. The "Enroll in Creator Program" funnel CTA on `/search?category=services` will not appear until SuperAdmin sets the flag on the curated offerings.
- **No public press / launch plan** in repo. Founder/marketing-lead handover gap.

### General Counsel — Legal & Compliance

**Strong**
- Centralised legal-document system (`legal_documents` + `legal_document_acceptances`) with versioning + IP/UA/context capture is **the right primitive** and already covers Voice Marketplace ToS §9a.
- Per-program creator terms scaffolded (`program_video_terms`, `program_voice_terms`, `program_services_terms`).

**Risks (go-live blockers)**
- **Placeholder terms text.** `0036_creator_programs.sql` seeds three program-terms documents whose body is literally `"Placeholder ... program terms. Update via the legal admin UI before going live."` **Block:** real lawyer-reviewed text must replace the placeholders before the wizard goes to creators.
- **§9b–§9f ToS additions still Open (#179).** Course Creator, Cert Issuance, SCORM Licensing, Writer Partner, Affiliate Network — all need text + acceptance flows. Not Day-1 if those products are deferred (see CPO).
- **Candidate share consent + GDPR audit (#186) Open.** Required for EU/UK/California operation if the agency redacted-share feature ships.
- **Content reporting / abuse path (#152) Open.** No user-facing way to report spam, impersonation, or inappropriate content. Required for any UGC platform under §230 / DSA.
- **Cookie consent + privacy preferences** exist (`privacyPreferences` table, cookie-preferences migration 0025) but the granular consent UX has not been audited against EU/UK requirements.

### CISO — Security & Trust

**Strong**
- Passkeys / WebAuthn (#65) implemented natively without external libs.
- OAuth providers wired for Google, LinkedIn, GitHub, Microsoft — secrets in Cloudflare env, no leaked credentials in repo.
- API keys hashed with SHA-256, key shown once.
- Password expiry (90d) + history (PBKDF2 last-5) + magic links.
- `ApiClient` Zod-validates every response (caught the `isCreator` strip bug in this session).

**Risks**
- **No external pen test** in repo. SOC 2 / SSO / data residency are listed as roadmap, not on Pricing.tsx — fine for SMB launch but blocks any enterprise deal.
- **Secret rotation procedure** not documented.
- **Webhook signature verification** is implemented per-provider (Stripe, Helcim, Dropbox Sign) but lacks a consolidated audit / replay-attack test.
- **Rate limiting** beyond AI metering: not visible. Auth endpoints, signup, magic-link request — none have visible per-IP rate limits.
- **Single-region DB** (see CTO) is also a security/availability concern for compliance frameworks that require geographic redundancy.

### Top 10 Hard Go-Live Blockers (cross-functional)

In priority order — these are the items that, if shipped open, expose the company to revenue loss, legal liability, or material UX failure on Day 1.

| # | Blocker | Owner | Gap ref |
|---|---------|-------|---------|
| 1 | Replace placeholder creator-program terms with lawyer-reviewed text | GC | #190, #179 |
| 2 | Ship the min-payout-threshold release worker (cron). Onboarding + ledger + Helcim ACH + Tremendous closed via #771 / #772; worker is the only thing still blocking funds movement. | CFO/CTO | #773 |
| 3 | Add 1099-NEC / W-8BEN / VAT collection for paying creators (W-9 / W-8BEN inputs encrypted-at-rest via #772; year-end reporting pipeline still missing) | CFO | #777 |
| 4 | Decide & flip `isPlatformService=true` on curated marketplace funnel offerings | CMO/CPO | #194 |
| 5 | Smoke-level integration test pack for auth/billing/resume/job/creator opt-in | CTO | #1 |
| 6 | Content abuse reporting path (`POST /api/reports`) | GC | #152 |
| 7 | Sales tax + VAT MOSS on token packs and subscription | CFO | (new gap) |
| 8 | Replace `#96` enrichment-credits stub OR feature-flag the marketing | CFO | #96 |
| 9 | Per-IP rate limiting on auth + magic-link + signup | CISO | (new gap) |
| 10 | DB backup/restore runbook + on-call escalation doc | CTO | (new gap) |

### Recommended Phased Launch

- **Phase 0 (now → 2 weeks)** — clear blockers 1, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10. Soft-launch to a beta cohort of paying Pro users only; creator monetisation initially limited to Articles (which need no payout rail until #172).
- **Phase 1 (2 → 8 weeks)** — Stripe Connect onboarding + min-payout-threshold worker (CFO blocker), Voice / Services creator monetisation flows, courses foundation (#160) on top of Studio reuse.
- **Phase 2 (8 → 16 weeks)** — SCORM 1.2 export (#161), Partner Program payouts (#172–#175), real-time chat (#41), enterprise/SSO if a customer pulls.

### LinkedIn-Comparable Scorecard

The CxO scorecard above measures absolute operational readiness. This second scorecard re-frames against the actual market comparable — **LinkedIn** — under the platform's positioning as "an HR-vertical marketing platform with native creator monetisation." Score = our capability ÷ LinkedIn's capability.

| Role | Score | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **CHRO** | **70%** | Recruiter parity surprisingly close — Boolean search (#70), saved searches, AI sourcing agent (#66), talent pool, ATS connectors (Greenhouse/Lever/Workday + merge.dev planned), sponsored job listings, seat-based company billing all in. Gaps vs LinkedIn Recruiter: depth of network graph (1B profiles) and "talent insights" market-report tier. |
| **CPO** | **55%** | Profiles, feed, messaging, jobs, articles, videos, ads-manager hierarchy (#108–#111), AI CHRO copilot, polymorphic reviews/boosts/feed-subjects all present. Missing vs LinkedIn: Learning (#160 in motion), Events, Newsletters, Sales Navigator. **Where we exceed:** every content type carries native rev-share at 95/5; LinkedIn pays creators $0 by default. |
| **CRO** | **45%** | Self-serve Pro subscription + token packs + 20% annual + 14-day trial + churn flow + paid placements (#106–#108) + ATS integrations + white-label demo lead form + ROI calculator. Missing: Sales-Navigator-style intent-data tier, multi-tier Recruiter Lite/Pro/Corporate matrix, large-account contract motion. |
| **CISO** | **35%** | Passkeys/WebAuthn native, OAuth ×4 providers, API keys SHA-256, password expiry/history, JWT + magic links, Zod-validated responses, Cloudflare WAF/DDoS by default. Missing vs LinkedIn-grade: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 attestations, formal pen-test cycle, public bug bounty, security-incident runbook. |
| **CFO** | **35%** | Modern subscription billing (Stripe + Helcim), token-pack metering, ad revenue tracking, seat-based company billing, AccessPolicy/BillingFacade split. Missing vs LinkedIn (which inherits Microsoft's SAP-grade backbone): Stripe Connect for creator payouts, 1099-NEC / W-8BEN, sales tax + VAT MOSS, multi-currency pricing, revenue-recognition automation. |
| **CTO** | **25%** | Edge-native architecture (Cloudflare Workers + Hyperdrive Postgres + R2) is more modern than LinkedIn's monolith. TS strict, OpenAPI 3.1 public, structured logging, polymorphic schema patterns. Cannot match: 20 years of ML pipelines, real-time feed ranking, multi-region datastores, content-moderation ML stack, search infra at 1B-profile scale. |
| **CMO** | **25%** | Marketing pages internally consistent, AI CHRO branding coherent, SEO content engine + auto-guides shipped. Cannot match: brand recognition (zero vs LinkedIn's "Microsoft trust halo"), 1B-user social proof, B2B ad-network footprint. |
| **CEO** | **20% raw / 95% on wedge** | **Raw market position 20%** — LinkedIn has 20 years of network-effect moat + Microsoft distribution. **Strategic wedge 95%** — creator rev-share + AI CHRO + course/training-material authoring is genuinely defensible because LinkedIn cannot pay creators or pivot to AI-native authoring without cannibalising its own ad-funded model. The structural conflict is the moat. |
| | | |
| **Avg (capability)** | **~40%** | We're at ~40% of LinkedIn's surface area with **one axis** where we structurally exceed them. |
| **Wedge defensibility** | **95%** | LinkedIn cannot easily flip to paying creators without breaking its ad business, nor pivot to AI-native course authoring without cannibalising LinkedIn Learning's instructor-fee model. Two reinforcing structural conflicts. |

**Three things hired.video does that LinkedIn structurally won't copy:**
1. **95/5 creator rev-share** on every monetisable content type (articles, voice clones, video templates, services, courses). LinkedIn pays creators $0 by default.
2. **AI CHRO as the headline product surface** — UX built around the AI, not bolted on.
3. **Studio-as-authoring-tool** — the same engine that produces a 30-second job pitch produces a 10-minute training course (see Training Materials & SCORM section above). LinkedIn Learning still relies on instructor-uploaded video without AI-native authoring.

**Three things LinkedIn has that no amount of code closes the gap on:**
1. **Network effect** — 1B profiles of professional-graph data.
2. **Microsoft distribution** — Teams / Outlook / Office integration.
3. **Enterprise security posture** — SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / dedicated security org / public bug bounty. Achievable for us, but a 12–18-month investment.

**Practical implication for marketing:** every surface should lead with **"keep 95% of what you make"** as the headline — not feature parity claims. The wedge collapses if creators don't actually receive money, so the CFO blocker (Stripe Connect + payout pipeline) becomes the single most important capability to ship.

## Consolidated Gap Register

Single source of truth for **open + partial + removed** items. Add a new entry to the bottom of the value tier it belongs to (see **Ordering** below); status changes happen in place. The bulk of `✅ Done` history is summarized in the [Done — Shipped Capability Summary](#done--shipped-capability-summary) above; Done rows that still carry useful detail are collected in the Resolved sections at the very bottom.

**Phases:** `Now` = 0–30 days · `Soon` = 30–60 days · `Mid` = 60–120 days · `Later` = 6–12 months

**Types:** `billing` = revenue enforcement · `feature` = product capability · `arch` = architecture · `quality` = code quality · `legacy` = legacy parity · `bug` = defect · `perf` = performance

**Ordering:** active entries are grouped into four value tiers — **T1 Direct Revenue**, **T2 Conversion & Activation**, **T3 Retention & Growth**, **T4 Cost / Quality / Arch** — then sorted within each tier by Priority → Phase → Status → id. Resolved items (✅ Done / Removed / Won't-fix / Superseded) are collected at the bottom. Tiering is heuristic (type + title keywords); move a row between tiers by editing it if the call is wrong.

**Current totals (recounted 2026-05-30 — post Snap! visual block editor pass; +2 from the Builderforce SDK 0.8.2 traceId pass #1810/#1811): 632 active — T1 76 · T2 51 · T3 328 · T4 193 — plus 352 ✅ Done and 20 closed/superseded archived at the bottom. A future contributor wiring a new AI tool the old way (raw `callLLMWithUsage`, no wrap) would not break a single test even though they'd be silently re-introducing the leak. Fix: add a generic test helper that calls every AI route once with a stub LLM that returns deterministic usage, then asserts `recordTokenUsage` (or its mock) was invoked exactly once with the matching `featureKey` + `totalTokens`. | 511 | 🔲 Open | Soon | P2 | `feature` | **Gateway-internal retry billing semantics unspecified — risk of double-counting tokens against our user-side ledger** (2026-05-09) | The SDK response carries `_builderforce.retries: number` indicating how many times the gateway internally retried before returning a successful response. If the gateway charges the tenant key for each upstream attempt (typical pricing model), the `usage` we record from the final response captures all retries. We then debit that amount once on `tokenLedger.charge` — fine. BUT if the gateway returns 5xx after exhausting its internal retries AND we then advance to the NEXT profile in our cross-vendor chain (which the gateway doesn't know is a logically related call), the tenant has paid for both the failed retry burst AND the new profile's tokens. Our user-side ledger only sees the final successful charge. Result: tenant key spend > sum of user-side debits = gap. Fix: gateway documents whether `usage` on success includes retry tokens (yes/no), and whether failed-but-retried attempts are billed (yes/no). Builderforce SDK could expose `_builderforce.retryUsage[]` so our adapter can choose to debit each gateway retry separately. Until clarified: SA dashboard will under-report user-side spend vs tenant-key spend by the gateway-internal-retry delta. |

| 1802 | 🔲 Open | Later | P3 | `quality` | **`useCanvasHistory` sidecar captures on commit but never seeds the initial checkpoint sidecar** (opened 2026-05-30 during #592 closure). [useCanvasHistory](hired.video/frontend/lib/studio/editor-v2/use-canvas-history.ts) starts with `checkpointSidecarRef.current = undefined` and only populates it when a commit fires. If the user makes one edit then undoes back below the first edit, the restore path sees `undefined` and skips the sidecar — selection stays wherever it last was instead of resetting to "scene 0". For typical sessions this never bites (the user can't undo past the project's loaded state), but `reset()` callers that pre-populate selection via separate setters won't see selection restored via undo from the loaded state. Fix: invoke `sidecarRef.current?.capture()` once during initial render OR in `reset()` before clearing the stacks. Already mitigated by the `if (sidecar !== undefined) restore(...)` guard, but worth seeding for correctness. |
| 1803 | 🔲 Open | Soon | P3 | `feature` | **PLATFORM_PRESETS Pro-only gating is advertised but not enforced — `youtube-4k60` / `vimeo-prores-master` / `broadcast-1080i` reach the render facade without an entitlement check** (opened 2026-05-30 during #342 closure). [export-profiles.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/timeline/export-profiles.ts) ships `proOnly: true` on three presets. `ExportProfilePicker` paints a lock badge + disables the click handler when `proLocked` is true. But the render facade itself doesn't enforce entitlement — a caller that wires the picker without setting `proLocked` (or that constructs a `PlatformExportProfile` programmatically) can ship a 4K export on a free account. Fix: extend `renderTimeline` to check `opts.platformProfile.proOnly && !opts.isPro` and throw a `PRO_REQUIRED` error, mirroring the existing `requirePro("4K export")` middleware pattern on the server. Pairs with the #283 ProRes/DNxHR export work. |
| 1804 | 🔲 Open | Later | P4 | `perf` | **NLE bin folder rename does a workspace-scoped LIKE scan — fine at 100 sources, sluggish at 10K** (opened 2026-05-30 during #358 closure). The new `POST /api/nle/sources/folders/rename` matches via `binFolder = from OR binFolder LIKE 'from/%'`. Postgres can use the existing `(user_id, bin_folder)` index for the equality branch but the `LIKE 'prefix/%'` branch needs a `text_pattern_ops` index to be fully indexed. At workspace sizes today (<1K sources/user) this is fine; at 10K+ it becomes a sequential scan within the workspace. Fix when bin volumes get there: add a `text_pattern_ops` index on `nle_media_sources.bin_folder` and verify the LIKE branch hits it. Not blocking. |

To close: stand up a Cloudflare Durable Object per conversation (or a single chat-room DO keyed by `conversationId`), add a `WebSocketPair` upgrade handler at `/api/chat/socket/:id`, broadcast `message`, `typing`, `presence` events, and migrate the frontend `chat` panel from polling to a `useChannel(conversationId)` hook. Durable Objects are the right fit because they already underpin the worker runtime and have built-in WebSocket hibernation — no Redis required for a v1. Unblocks: parity claim on the competitors page, lower latency on AI chat panel, presence indicators on Comm Hub. |

Full PRD at [docs/prd/bookings-and-reservations.md](hired.video/docs/prd/bookings-and-reservations.md) — covers data model (9 tables), provisioning bridge, API surface, calendar sync, Stripe Connect take-rate, 5-phase rollout. **Unblocks**: (a) Creator persona becomes monetizable beyond ad-supported content and token-pricing tiers; (b) opens the senior-exec fractional / advisory bookings track (#1627) without needing recruiter sourcing infrastructure; (c) gives BurnRateOS a high-value B2B-ops module that pairs with the contact-sourcing module to form a real operator OS; (d) is reused by every audience that wants 1:1 monetization — career coaches, resume coaches, mentors, technical consultants, fitness coaches, fractional CxOs. |

| 1631 | 🔲 Open | Soon | P3 | `feature` | **UnifiedSearch query is exact-substring only — no typo tolerance / stemming / synonyms** (opened 2026-05-26 alongside the static-fetcher push-down fix that made `/?q=research` return the Employer Research tool + the "How to Use the Employer Research Tool" blog post). After this pass, each per-type static fetcher in [card-feed.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/card-feed.ts) filters its in-memory catalogue with a lowercased substring match BEFORE pagination — without this, the recency sort buried relevant articles off page 1 (first 2 articles fetched were always the newest by `publishedAt`, even when none matched the query). `matchesNeedle` is intentionally simple — it doesn't tolerate typos (`reserach` → `research`), doesn't stem (`researching` → `research`), and has no synonym table (`employer` ↔ `company`, `salary` ↔ `compensation` ↔ `pay`, `research` ↔ `audit` ↔ `review`). All three are real user expectations on a search box that says "Search" not "Exact substring search". **Fix path**: (a) cheap win — handcrafted synonym map in `card-feed.ts` for the top ~30 employment-domain pairs, applied on both sides of the match; (b) fuzzy match — wire Fuse.js or a manual Levenshtein-distance-2 check against title/name so single-character typos still hit; (c) stemming — Porter stemmer is ~3kB and tolerates `-ing` / `-ed` / `-s`. None of these are in place today; the current pass deliberately scoped to "fix the literal-match case for the article the user named" and left these as the obvious follow-ups. **Adjacent**: the same fetchers ignore Unicode normalisation, so an accented input or a smart quote doesn't normalise to its ASCII equivalent — surfaces when international content lands on the platform (#1148). |

| 1570 | 🔲 Open | Now | P1 | `bug` | **AI dispatch chain blows itself up when Cerebras rejects a Zod-derived JSON schema, then Cloudflare subrequest cap kills the remaining failovers** (opened 2026-05-26 from a live `AI_UNAVAILABLE` 503, `correlationId=llm-2cc6ba1b-34e8-4024-ada0-b8b55e3f1798`). Two coupled failures: **(1) Builderforce-side schema-translation bug.** [llm-client.ts deriveJsonSchema](hired.video/api/src/services/adapters/llm-client.ts#L518-L533) hands `toJSONSchema(zodSchema)` to the gateway as `JsonSchemaSpec { strict: true, schema }`. Zod emits `maxLength` on every `z.string().max(N)`, but Cerebras's strict-schema validator rejects `maxLength` on `type: "string"` (`400 invalid_request_error / wrong_api_format: Invalid fields for schema with types ['string']: {'maxLength'}`). The gateway's job per [llm-client.ts:7-12](hired.video/api/src/services/adapters/llm-client.ts#L7-L12) — *"Vendor identity is invisible to route code"* — includes translating JSON-Schema dialects per vendor. Today it forwards the schema verbatim, so the first two Cerebras-routed profiles in the fallback chain die before the model even runs. Fix belongs in `@seanhogg/builderforce-sdk` / the gateway worker: strip Cerebras-incompatible keys (`maxLength`, `minLength`, possibly `pattern`/`format`) before forwarding to that vendor. **(2) hired.video-side subrequest exhaustion.** Once the first two attempts burn subrequests, attempts 3–6 all return `Too many subrequests by single Worker invocation` (Cloudflare's per-invocation cap — 50 on free, 1000 on paid). The dispatch loop in [llm-client.ts dispatch](hired.video/api/src/services/adapters/llm-client.ts#L588-L721) does one `fetch` per profile in the chain, and any subrequests the route already spent on auth + budget check + token-ledger reads + KV reads + Sentry breadcrumbs are competing for the same budget. To close on the hired.video side: (a) instrument subrequest counts per request via a Hono middleware so we can see which routes are near the cap; (b) consider trimming the fallback chain for use cases whose first vendor frequently 400s on schema (`USE_CASE_PROFILES` in [providers.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/adapters/providers.ts)) since a 5-profile chain inside an already-subrequest-heavy route is structurally fragile; (c) short-term band-aid until Builderforce ships the schema translator — audit Zod schemas used in Cerebras-routed `useCase` profiles and drop `.max(N)` from string fields. **Adjacent**: gap #515 already flags silent gateway substitution for latency-pinned `match`; #525 already shrank free-tier per-attempt timeouts. **Unblocks**: the entire AI surface (resume scoring, match, Career 360, course generation, article moderation, chat agent) reliably completing under live Cerebras schema-validation regressions without taking down the rest of the dispatch chain. Primary fix is upstream in builderforce.ai; mitigation work tracked here. |

For rows where `content.metaData` carries embedded media descriptors (data URIs, large skillEvidence arrays from #1349 / [[project_skill_evidence]], or legacy AI-parse residuals), the walk is O(content-size) and dominates worker CPU. **(c) `c.json(result.body)` runs `JSON.stringify` over the full normalized blob** — content fields like `metaData`, `skillEvidence`, and the new `meta.template` bag can balloon to several MB on heavy users; even at canonical shape, the serialize step is unavoidable per-request. **Fix plan**: (1) **DB**: add `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS resume_information_slug_idx ON resume_information (slug) WHERE slug IS NOT NULL` as a new migration — partial-index since most rows have a UUID-derived slug, but the conditional keeps the index small. (2) **Read-path normalization**: short-circuit `normalizeContent` when the stored row is already canonical — detect by checking whether any top-level key starts with an uppercase character; if not, return the input plus default-array fills without walking. The PascalCase normalization is only meaningful for legacy hired.video JSON-Resume exports that haven't been re-saved since the migration — i.e. a vanishingly small share of read traffic. (3) **Payload diet**: audit what `content.metaData` and `content.skillEvidence` look like on the affected slug (`seanhogg`) — if they're carrying base64 media or 1000+ evidence rows, ship a one-time backfill that moves media references to the existing `metaData` media-attachment endpoint and dedupes skillEvidence. (4) **Diagnostic**: instrument [handleGetResume](hired.video/api/src/services/resume/ResumeService.ts) to emit `console.warn("[resumes/get] large content", { resumeId, contentSize, slug })` when stringified content exceeds 256 KB so we can tell whether (b) or (c) is the dominant cost. **Adjacent**: gap #979 already flags the 30 s worker CPU budget as fragile for any sync-fanout flow; gap #1570 documents the per-invocation subrequest cap. This one is the read-side analog. **Unblocks**: every embedded resume on every public profile + Chrome-extension embed + social-feed card — the embed has been silently 5XXing for every user whose content blob crossed the size threshold. |

| 1220 | ⏳ In Progress | Soon | P1 | `bug` | **CI deploy pipeline silently masks `db:push` failures, so SQL migrations apply onto a partially-bootstrapped DB and FK constraints to Drizzle-only tables fail** (opened 2026-05-25 — surfaced when [migration 0117](hired.video/api/drizzle/0117_recruiter_agent_followups.sql) deploy errored with `relation "recruiter_agent_runs" does not exist` despite the migration's defensive `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`). [.github/workflows/ci.yml](hired.video/.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs `db:push` (Drizzle schema sync) THEN `run-sql-migrations.mjs`. When `db:push` fails (e.g. [migration 0046](hired.video/api/drizzle/0046_sourcing_marketplace.sql) hit PostgreSQL's 1600-column limit on `job_items` because the out-of-tree legacy bootstrap left it bloated — see #1203), Drizzle-only tables like `recruiter_agent_runs`/`live_screening_sessions` never get created. SQL migrations then fail downstream with cryptic FK errors that look like the migration's fault. **Partial fix shipped 2026-05-25:** (i) [0117 hardened](hired.video/api/drizzle/0117_recruiter_agent_followups.sql) with a guarded DO-block FK addition so it survives this scenario; (ii) the four obsolete sourcing columns 0046 was adding to `job_items` (`accepts_sourcing_bids` / `sourcing_fee_cents` / `sourcing_deadline` / `sourcing_terms`) were dead — 0052 immediately drops them in favour of [`job_sourcing_listings`](hired.video/api/src/services/recruiter-marketplace/SourcingListingService.ts), and zero consumers remained across api/src/, shared/, or frontend/ — so they've been removed from 0046, taking the column-bloat blocker out of the deploy path. **Second fix shipped 2026-05-25** (after 0121's `archived_at` add on `job_items` hit the same 1600-column wall on the next deploy): (1) `run-sql-migrations.mjs` now tracks applied migrations in a runner-owned `_sql_migrations` table — each file runs at most once per database, eliminating the previous "replay every file every deploy" loop that made the `IF NOT EXISTS` defensive layer load-bearing; (2) [migration 0122](hired.video/api/drizzle/0122_reclaim_job_items_columns.sql) runs `VACUUM FULL "job_items"` to reclaim the dropped column slots — runs exactly once because the new runner records it as applied on success; (3) the failing `job_items.archived_at` add was extracted from 0121 into [migration 0123](hired.video/api/drizzle/0123_job_items_archived_at.sql) so it lands AFTER the slot reclamation; (4) [0121](hired.video/api/drizzle/0121_taxonomies_archive_versions.sql) had the broken `ALTER TABLE "job_items" ADD COLUMN "archived_at"` block excised with a header note pointing to 0122/0123. **Still open:** (a) make `db:push` failures fatal in CI by adding `set -e` and explicit exit-code propagation around the drizzle call (currently only the SQL-migrations step has `set -e`), (c) audit every Drizzle-only table in [KNOWN_MISSING_CREATE_TABLE](hired.video/api/scripts/migration-schema-parity.test.mjs) for downstream FK consumers and prepend defensive CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in those consumer migrations the same way 0117 now does. Unblocks deploys against fresh / partial DBs without manual SQL intervention. |
| 742 | 🔲 Open | Soon | P1 | `bug` | **Rendered MP4 doesn't match the editor's Preview output** (2026-05-17 — reported by sean@: "the VIDEO that is being generated also doesnt match the version showin in the preview") | **Architectural finding on closer inspection (2026-05-17):** the per-frame canvas render path is ALREADY unified — both [VideoPreview.tsx::drawFrame](hired.video/frontend/components/VideoPreview.tsx) (RAF) and [video-exporter.ts::WebCodecs loop](hired.video/frontend/lib/renderer/video-exporter.ts) call the same `render(ctx, compiledVideo, time)` from [frame-renderer.ts](hired.video/frontend/lib/renderer/frame-renderer.ts). The only divergence flag is `{ previewMode: true }` which suppresses the first-scene watermark in preview only. So the drift the user reported is NOT scene-graph divergence; it's in three async-asset / audio subsystems that the export doesn't synchronize with the preview's state: **(1) Font loading** — preview waits across RAF ticks for `document.fonts.ready`; the export's synchronous frame loop runs once and moves on, so glyphs render via fallback fonts if a webfont hasn't loaded by frame 0. **(2) Image assets** — `<img>` nodes inside scenes load async; preview eventually paints them as their `naturalWidth` materializes, the export captures a single frame per timestamp with no retry. **(3) Audio pipeline** — WebCodecs path muxes silence (no audio path at all); MediaRecorder fallback builds its OWN WebAudio graph in `exportMediaRecorderWithAudio` instead of consuming the shared [useMusicScheduler](hired.video/frontend/lib/audio/use-music-scheduler.ts) that #720 unified for preview. Concrete fix bundle: (a) `await document.fonts.ready` + walk every node in the compiled scenes to `await ImageDecoder.decode()` before the frame loop starts; (b) for the WebCodecs path, append an AudioTrack to the mux using a captured render of the shared music scheduler (offline AudioContext for determinism); (c) drop the bespoke MediaRecorder audio mixer and route through the same scheduler. Was originally framed as a renderer rewrite — the actual fix is much narrower. Unblocks: external MP4 publishes match the editor preview exactly. |

| 1810 | 🔲 Open | Soon | P3 | `quality` | **Gateway `traceId` is surfaced on the success path but NOT on the failure path — `LLMDispatchError` still reports a locally-minted `correlationId` (`llm-${crypto.randomUUID()}`) instead of the gateway's authoritative trace** (opened 2026-05-30 while wiring `_builderforce.traceId` from Builderforce SDK 0.8.2 into API responses). On success, [llm-client.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/adapters/llm-client.ts) now threads `_builderforce.traceId` through `LLMUsage.traceId` → `toClientUsage` → the chat + course-generate responses. On failure, `dispatch()` throws `LLMDispatchError` carrying a *client-generated* `correlationId` that was sent **to** the gateway as request metadata — which is NOT the same id the gateway records as its trace. Per the SDK docs the gateway's trace on the error path is `BuilderforceApiError.details.correlationId`; we never read it. Result: a user hitting a 503/502 cannot quote an id that Builderforce support can resolve server-side (the success path can). Fix: in `classifyAttemptError`, capture `(err.details as {correlationId?: string})?.correlationId` onto `LLMDispatchAttempt`, and prefer the gateway trace over the local id when building `LLMDispatchError` (keep the local id only as a fallback for pre-dispatch/non-Builderforce throws). Unblocks: support can trace failed AI calls, not just successful ones. |

| 1522 | ✅ Done | Now | P1 | `bug` | **Seeded `md5(slug)::uuid` IDs fail Zod 4 `.uuid()` validation — every route that strict-validated a DB-row UUID rejected seed-derived rows** (opened + fully fixed 2026-05-26 after a support ticket: PATCH `/api/courses/enrollments/:id/progress` returned 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` "Invalid UUID" with body `{ lessonId: "c87f7656-673a-7756-d100-281032a50731", … }` — that lesson is from [0131_seed_platform_learning_library.sql](hired.video/api/drizzle/0131_seed_platform_learning_library.sql) which uses `md5('seed-lesson:…')::uuid` for deterministic IDs). Root cause: Zod 4's `.uuid()` regex requires the variant nibble to be `[89abAB]` (RFC 4122), but MD5 hashes land on any nibble — the user's lesson ID has variant `d`. Same seed pattern is in [0113_so_you_want_to_become_articles.sql](hired.video/api/drizzle/0113_so_you_want_to_become_articles.sql) for seeded articles. **Fix**: introduced `UuidLikeSchema` + `UUID_LIKE_REGEX` in [shared/validation.ts](hired.video/shared/validation.ts) (permissive 8-4-4-4-12 hex, no version/variant constraint) and **swept the entire codebase** — 270 call sites across 57 files in `api/src/` + `shared/` migrated from `z.string().uuid()` → `UuidLikeSchema` (the two custom-message callers in [superadmin/sessions.ts](hired.video/api/src/routes/superadmin/sessions.ts) + [superadmin/users.ts](hired.video/api/src/routes/superadmin/users.ts) preserve their messages via `z.string().regex(UUID_LIKE_REGEX, "…")`). Strict `UuidSchema` is kept in shared/validation.ts for IDs generated fresh in app code; doc comment in the file pins the split. **Latent Zod-4 bug also fixed in the same pass**: two `z.record(z.unknown())` calls in [courses.ts](hired.video/api/src/routes/courses.ts) (ScormCommitSchema.cmi, XapiStatementSchema.context) were silently broken under Zod 4 (which requires `z.record(key, value)`); both now `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`. **Pre-existing fixture bug fixed in the same pass**: [resume-contract.test.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/__tests__/resume-contract.test.ts) was missing `archivedAt: null` on its base fixture; added. **Tests added** (3 new test files + 1 shared fixture module, 72 cases total — closes the test-coverage gap that masked this bug): (a) [shared/__tests__/validation.test.ts](hired.video/shared/__tests__/validation.test.ts) — 25 cases pinning `UuidSchema` strict + `UuidLikeSchema` permissive + raw regex against the prod-incident UUID, runtime v4s, RFC v1/v7, nil/max, uppercase, shape-length drift, non-hex, whitespace, null/undefined/numbers; (b) [api/src/routes/__tests__/courses-schemas.test.ts](hired.video/api/src/routes/__tests__/courses-schemas.test.ts) — 38 cases against `ProgressUpdateSchema`, `ScormCommitSchema`, `XapiStatementSchema`, `PrerequisiteSchema`, `CreateLessonSchema` (happy + boundary + exception, with explicit md5-seed-derived UUID fixtures); (c) [api/src/routes/__tests__/learning-paths-schemas.test.ts](hired.video/api/src/routes/__tests__/learning-paths-schemas.test.ts) — 9 cases against `AttachCourseSchema`; (d) [shared/__tests__/uuid-fixtures.ts](hired.video/shared/__tests__/uuid-fixtures.ts) — DRY fixture module (`V4_UUID`, `SEED_DERIVED_UUID`, `V1_UUID`, `V7_UUID_RFC`, `NIL_UUID`, `MAX_UUID`, `SYNTHETIC_V4_UUID`, `SHAPE_FAILURES`) consumed by all four test files including the pre-existing scorecards `schemas.test.ts`. | 1590 | ✅ Done | — | — | `bug` | **apiClient retried server-side failures with exponential backoff, amplifying a CPU-exhausted worker's load by 4×** (closed 2026-05-26 alongside the save-draft 503 sweep). [api-client.ts request loop](hired.video/frontend/lib/api-client.ts) used to retry every error except ValidationError / AuthenticationError / AuthorizationError on the assumption that everything else was a transient transport problem. In practice that meant any HTTP 5xx (incl. the Worker 503s under CPU pressure) got hit 4 times per user — the wrangler-tail 503 firehose at 2026-05-26T21:24:30Z+ on `/api/resumes/embedded` was 1Hz, matching the 1s/2s/4s/10s exponential-backoff retry from this loop. Fix: only retry when the failure looks like a true transport problem (no HTTP response — `httpStatus` absent in normalized error context AND no `HTTP \d{3}:` prefix on the message). Any server-emitted response, including 503, is now terminal. Closes the amplification side of the save-draft 503 incident. |

Microsoft codes (AADSTS70000/AADSTS50173/AADSTS50076/interaction_required/consent_required/login_required) now route to the reauth banner instead of the 502 toast. **Original:** **`MAILBOX_REAUTH_REQUIRED` is detected via a regex match on Google's `invalid_grant` substring — Microsoft Graph returns at least three more codes (`AADSTS70000`, `interaction_required`, `consent_required`) that today's classifier mis-routes to the generic `REFRESH_FAILED` 502 toast** (opened 2026-05-21 — surfaced fixing the Gmail-specific case at [email-integration.ts /accounts/:id/access-token](hired.video/api/src/routes/email-integration.ts)) | [refreshAccessToken in oauth.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/email-integration/oauth.ts) throws an `Error` whose message is the raw provider response body. | 1578 | ✅ Done | Now | P1 | `bug` | **`POST /api/ai/chat` 500 on `ai_chat_messages` insert — user-visible chat now resilient (best-effort persistence + early user-write), diagnostic surface live, root cause still pending next repro** (opened 2026-05-26 from two live INTERNAL_ERROR support tickets ~5 min apart, sessions `91a5a4dc-…` + `73993c7c-…`, same Career-Coach interview-practice prompt, identical `tokens_used: 5069`; reporter confirmed it 500s on **every** chat click before the fix below). What the user saw was the literal SQL of the failed insert prefixed with `Failed query: …` — i.e. Drizzle's wrapper message — with **zero PG error code, constraint, or detail**, because [globalErrorHandler](hired.video/api/src/middleware/errorHandler.ts) only forwarded `err.message` and dropped `err.cause`. Without the cause, we cannot tell whether the failure is (a) FK violation on `session_id` (most likely — session row never committed, or replica-lag race between the SELECT at [ai.ts:145-155](hired.video/api/src/routes/ai.ts#L145-L155) and the INSERT at [ai.ts:262](hired.video/api/src/routes/ai.ts#L262)), (b) a transient Neon HTTP write failure, or (c) a constraint we didn't anticipate. Schema itself is permissive — `content text` unbounded, `role varchar(20)` fits `"user"`, `tokens_used int4 nullable` fits 5069 — so a schema-level rejection is ruled out from the surfaced data. **Shipped this pass:** (1) [errorHandler.ts](hired.video/api/src/middleware/errorHandler.ts) now extracts PG diagnostic fields (`code`, `detail`, `hint`, `schema`, `table`, `column`, `dataType`, `constraint`, `routine`) from `err` + walks up to four levels of `err.cause`, attaches them as `_pg` on the response envelope, and includes them in the structured server log. (2) [errorSourceFilter.ts](hired.video/api/src/middleware/errorSourceFilter.ts) generalised from a `_source`-only stripper to a `SUPERADMIN_ONLY_ERROR_FIELDS` allowlist, so the new `_pg` field is SuperAdmin-only by the same rule. (3) Adjacent security gap closed in the same pass: the session-validation path at [ai.ts:145-155](hired.video/api/src/routes/ai.ts#L145-L155) now filters by `(id, userId)` instead of `id` alone — pre-fix, any authenticated user could POST a turn into another user's session by guessing/observing the UUID, leaking content + corrupting their history. (4) **User-visible chat fix:** the two `ai_chat_messages` inserts now go through a single `persistChatMessage(role, content, tokensUsed)` helper at [ai.ts](hired.video/api/src/routes/ai.ts) (DRY — one try/catch site, one log line shape). User message persists BEFORE the LLM dispatch (when subrequest budget is still flush — see #1570 for the dispatch chain's per-invocation cost); assistant message persists AFTER. Both are wrapped in try/catch — failure logs `[ai/chat] persist message failed` with `{sessionId, role, tokensUsed, err}` and **does not 500 the route**. Chat appears to work even when persistence is broken; the history just loses that turn (recoverable: the LLM-generated answer is in the response body, the user's prompt is still in the request body the client just sent). Dead `let model = "mock"` (assigned but never read) dropped while restructuring. **Still open:** root cause — wait for the next `console.error("[ai/chat] persist message failed", …)` log with the new `_pg` surface live to confirm whether the failure class is FK / replica-lag / transient / subrequest-cap-exhaustion, then either (i) wrap session-resolve + message-insert in a Neon HTTP transaction so they share a connection + snapshot (FK race), (ii) retry once on Neon transient classes, or (iii) trim USE_CASE_PROFILES["chat"] / strip non-essential middleware off this route to free subrequests (#1570 root cause). **Out of scope this pass (recorded):** `tokens_used: 5069` for a ~2 KB visible prompt looks high but is plausibly correct — it's `result.usage.promptTokens` from the LLM at [ai.ts:227](hired.video/api/src/routes/ai.ts#L227), which includes the system prompt + last 20 history messages loaded at [ai.ts:175-183](hired.video/api/src/routes/ai.ts#L175-L183); not worth changing without a confirmed mis-count from the gateway. **Adjacent:** the diagnostic improvement here helps every DB-layer 500 across the API, not just AI chat. |

| 1651 | ❎ Deferred-by-design | — | — | `perf` | **Counter recompute incremental triggers — deferred** (resolved 2026-05-26). The daily UPDATE-with-IS-DISTINCT-FROM in [counter-recompute.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/maintenance/counter-recompute.ts) is O(N) once per day and only touches drifted rows; per-insert/delete triggers are O(1) per write but pay overhead on EVERY write — and write volume on the source tables (artifact_views, candidate_submissions, etc.) is far higher than read volume on the counters. Daily reconcile is the cheaper shape at current and projected scale. Switch when a single counter cache demonstrably crosses a measurable cost threshold (e.g. > 100M source rows AND > 1k counter-display reads/sec). Not happening at 1M users. | (opened 2026-05-26 from pass-9 scale audit). [services/maintenance/counter-recompute.ts](hired.video/api/src/services/maintenance/counter-recompute.ts) runs daily `UPDATE … SET col = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM source …)`. At 100M+ rows in the source table, the COUNT(*) is non-trivial. Per-insert/delete triggers are faster (O(1) per write vs O(N) once per day) but require migration of every counter. Switch when a single counter cache crosses a measurable cost threshold — for now the daily recompute is cheaper than the trigger overhead given low write rates. **Unblocks**: linear-write counters that stay accurate without a daily reconcile. |
